overview: Camptosaurus dispar was a stocky ornithopod from the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation (~155–145 Ma), reaching up to five metres. It could walk on two or four legs — its wrist structure allowed quadrupedal locomotion — and represents an intermediate form between the small bipedal hypsilophodontids and the large Iguanodon lineage. Camptosaurus is among the most common herbivores of the Morrison Formation.

Bone pathologies (healed injuries on ribs and limb bones) indicate Camptosaurus was a common prey item for Allosaurus. The injuries — bite marks and healed bone infections consistent with predator attack — provide direct evidence of predator-prey interactions in the Morrison ecosystem, complementing the famous Allosaurus-Stegosaurus interaction evidence.

articles.title: Discovery
articles.body: Named by Marsh in 1885 from Como Bluff material; the name "flexible lizard" refers to its curved femur. Multiple specimens are known from the Morrison Formation, making it one of the best-studied ornithopods from the Jurassic. A specimen from the Jurassic of England (C. prestwichii) has been reassigned to the genus Cumnoria.

articles.title: Facultative quadrupedalism
articles.body: Unlike hypsilophodontids, Camptosaurus had a robust wrist with adaptations allowing the hand to bear weight. It could rear up to feed from higher vegetation and drop to all fours for sustained locomotion. This flexibility anticipated the obligate quadrupedalism of Iguanodon and hadrosaurs.

articles.title: Predator-prey evidence
articles.body: Several Camptosaurus specimens show healed bite marks on ribs and limbs consistent with Allosaurus attack. One individual shows a healed bite wound on the ilium — the animal survived the attack. These pathologies, combined with the size difference between Camptosaurus and Allosaurus, suggest Camptosaurus was a regular prey item in Morrison food webs.

fossilRecord.material: Partial skeletons of a medium-sized ornithopod.
fossilRecord.paleo: Late Jurassic Morrison herbivore fauna with sauropods, stegosaurs and small ornithischians.
fossilRecord.evidence: Limb and jaw material support a bipedal to facultatively quadrupedal browsing ornithopod.

record.description: Camptosaurus dispar was a medium-sized ankylopollexian ornithopod from the Morrison Formation of western North America. Several partial skeletons and skulls document its anatomy, but many species and specimens historically assigned to Camptosaurus have been moved to other genera.
facts: The accepted genus concept is substantially narrower than in older books.
It was primarily bipedal and may have used the forelimbs in slow locomotion, but habitual gait is a functional inference.

review.ageReviewNote: Secure C. dispar material is Kimmeridgian-Tithonian in the Morrison Formation.
